comparison.summary: Against your priorities, Path A fits learning at 5 out of 5 and the long-term goal of hard ML problems, but it clashes with stability at 4 out of 5 during the first two to three years. Path B fits stability, earning, and growing ownership, but it leaves the top learning priority only partly met. In short, this is deep ML access now with debt risk, versus financial strength now with ML drift risk.
dominant_assumptions: Funding for Path A is unknown beyond $25K in savings. Tuition of about $60K a year plus Boston housing drives the $196K-$207K debt range at graduation in this world.

Path A assumes the degree, internship, and thesis convert into an ML engineer role soon after graduation. Pay in the grounded $120K-$135K range, rather than the higher compiled range, would slow debt paydown.
Path B assumes the Austin team gives little core ML work and that internal moves lead to platform work, not modeling work. A real ML rotation or sponsor team would change this world a lot.
what_would_change_my_mind: A scholarship, assistantship, or employer funding that cuts the roughly $120K tuition bill by a large share.
Clear proof the Austin job includes ML modeling work, a rotation, or a supported transfer path in the first 1-2 years.
A weak internship or thesis outcome in Boston, or no ML offer within a few months after graduation.

comparison.summary: Against your priorities, Path A fits learning at 5 out of 5 and the long-term goal of hard ML problems, but it clashes with stability at 4 out of 5 during the first two to three years. Path B fits stability, earning, and growing ownership, but it leaves the top learning priority only partly met. In short, this is deep ML access now with debt risk, versus financial strength now with ML drift risk.
dominant_assumptions: Funding for Path A is unknown beyond $25K in savings. Tuition of about $60K a year plus Boston housing drives the $196K-$207K debt range at graduation in this world.

Path A assumes the degree, internship, and thesis convert into an ML engineer role soon after graduation. Pay in the grounded $120K-$135K range, rather than the higher compiled range, would slow debt paydown.
Path B assumes the Austin team gives little core ML work and that internal moves lead to platform work, not modeling work. A real ML rotation or sponsor team would change this world a lot.
what_would_change_my_mind: A scholarship, assistantship, or employer funding that cuts the roughly $120K tuition bill by a large share.
Clear proof the Austin job includes ML modeling work, a rotation, or a supported transfer path in the first 1-2 years.
A weak internship or thesis outcome in Boston, or no ML offer within a few months after graduation.

messages.text: I'm a recent graduate interviewing for ML roles [ev_A_007] with my thesis plus summer internship project behind me [ev_A_005]. I completed a thesis on a hard ML problem [ev_A_023] and have ML engineer and scientist pipelines open [ev_A_006]. I graduated with no full-time offer [ev_A_020] and hold $196K to $207K in debt [ev_A_025], so on money I'm still unsure.

On stability, it was worth it for me. I'm full-time employed in Austin [ev_U_005] [ev_U_004] as a mid-level engineer on data platform [ev_B_005] earning $133K a year [ev_B_024] with $133K to $148K saved [ev_B_024]. I hear the money stress on your side, my side feels steadier as a solid saver in a stable role [ev_B_020], though I stayed exposed to reorgs and cuts [ev_B_017]. For learning it feels half-done, I'm a strong engineer but my ML goals are unmet [ev_B_023] after two years without deep ML practice [ev_B_013].

I hear you on steadier, my side feels different. I'm a recent graduate interviewing for ML roles [ev_A_007] with no full-time offer [ev_A_020]. I completed my thesis on a hard ML problem [ev_A_023] which fits my learning goal [ev_U_010], but I hold $196K to $207K in debt [ev_A_025] with high thesis and job uncertainty [ev_A_016].
